content.question: Why is K-fold cross-validation generally faster than leave-p-out cross-validation?
options: Because the computational load grows linearly with the number of folds - there are as many training iterations as there are folds, while leave-p-out requires far more iterations.
Because K-fold uses a smaller part of the dataset for training.
Because leave-p-out requires retraining the model within each fold.
Because K-fold does not require the model to be validated at all.
content.answer: Because the computational load grows linearly with the number of folds - there are as many training iterations as there are folds, while leave-p-out requires far more iterations.
